Definition: from a derivative of σύλλω (to strip; probably akin to G138; compare G4661); to despoil:--rob.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Corinthians he robbed other churches, taking wages from them to serve Corinth for free. He is not confessing a crime but turning the charge around: he stripped other congregations of their support so that Corinth would owe him nothing.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that a servant of Christ may go without his rights for the sake of the people he serves, and I hold that love, not payment, is what proves the ministry.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
